FXUS62 KRAH 131050
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
650 AM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Showers shift east of I-95 this morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 650 AM Sunday...

1) Showers will shift east of I-95 this morning. Partly sunny and 
warm this afternoon. Isolated showers this afternoon, mainly east.

2) Cooler and less humid with a NE flow much of this upcoming week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 228 AM Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Showers will shift east of I-95 this morning. 
Partly sunny this afternoon, only an isolated shower (10 percent). 

The base of the mid/upper level trough will pass overhead this 
morning. Subsidence in the rear of this feature will lower the 
shower chances to very isolated this afternoon (less than 10 percent 
at any one point). The exception may be along and east of I-95 where 
the showers may linger through late morning today. The main cold 
front will shift through the area this evening and overnight. This 
will be followed by cooler and drier advection from the northeast 
beginning Monday. Highs today will generally be in the mid to upper 
80s. Lows tonight in the mid 60s to around70. Highs Monday will be 
in the lower to mid 80s.

KEY MESSAGE 2... Cooler and less humid with a NE flow this 
upcoming week. 

Strong upper ridging is expected to set up over the Tennessee Valley 
early this week, then shift back westward toward the Southern Plains 
by Thursday and Friday. This will keep it dry this week over NC.

A 1030 mb surface high pressure will build down into the mid-
Atlantic states from the Great Lakes Monday, then slowly shift east 
off the New England coast by mid-week. The SW extension of the high 
will extend over NC keeping conditions dry and mild. Lows in the mid 
50s to lower 60s Monday through Thursday, with highs in the lower to 
mid 80s.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
As of 650 AM Sunday...

24 hour TAF period: Scattered showers through 14z will affect areas 
along the I-95 corridor from KFAY to KRWI. Otherwise, expect areas 
of low status and some fog through mid-morning, before lifting out. 
Winds will become light SW  to W this afternoon with VFR conditions.

Outlook: Generally VFR conditions are expected tonight through 
Monday and beyond this week as high pressure settles in.


&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

FXUS62 KILM 131047
AFDILM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Wilmington NC
647 AM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Expect lower rainfall chances with the higher PWAT environment 
shifting offshore today. Another Coastal Flood Advisory issued 
for high tide around Noon today for the lower Cape Fear 
River/downtown ILM.

Aviation section updated.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Deep Gulf moisture and a break in the ridge aloft will 
maintain some chances for showers and thunderstorms today.

2) A modified Canadian airmass will bring cooler temperatures and 
drier conditions to the area beginning Tuesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Deep Gulf moisture and a break in the ridge aloft 
will maintain some chances for showers and thunderstorms today.

After a quick initial round of some showers and isolated 
thunderstorms early this morning trends continue to suggest lower 
PoPs across the forecast area today. The impulse moving through 
early this morning will help to displace the high PWAT airmass off 
the coast. The coastal areas will have the best (albeit low) 
chances along the sea breeze this afternoon. Otherwise, 
temperatures will be well above normal today all locations, but 
that will be changing by Tuesday. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...A modified Canadian airmass will bring cooler 
temperatures and drier conditions to the area beginning Tuesday.

A cold front moving through Monday night will gradually allow 
for cooler and drier air to move across the forecast area 
Tuesday through mid-week. Moisture appears limited as the front
moves through thus only low PoPs will be included at this time.
High temperatures will likely be a a couple degrees below 
normal Tuesday and near seasonable Wednesday through Thursday. A
airmass will be much drier as well with some of the lower PWATs
that we have observed in a while. A few inland areas may see 
upper 50s, especially Tuesday night into early Wednesday 
morning.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
IFR restrictions across our inland areas will be patchy and 
intermittent over the next few hours before rising to VFR. 
Showers and storms will be limited to coastal terminals this 
afternoon, better chances along the Cape Fear. Maintained VCTS 
due to the anticipated brevity and limited coverage.

Extended Outlook...A low potential exists for some early morning 
stratus or fog affecting KLBT and KFLO late Sunday night into Monday 
morning. VFR conditions should prevail Monday through Wednesday as a 
more stable and drier Canadian airmass builds in from the north.

&&

.MARINE...
Sunday through Thursday...SWly flow will prevail today and tonight. 
The flow will begin to veer as a cold front approaches Monday.
As the front passes Monday night and a ridge of high pressure 
builds in from the north a NEly surge of winds will spread 
southward across the waters. This surge will likely result in 
Small Craft conditions that will extend into Tuesday. The NEly 
fetch will continue Wednesday but will gradually weaken by this 
time. A surface trough, or weak low, may approach the offshore 
waters from the E during Thursday, but confidence is very low 
at this time. Plan to continue with NEly winds across the 
waters Thursday until the picture becomes more clear. Seas will
build Monday night and with the fetch counter to the Gulf 
Stream conditions are expected to be fairly steep across the 
offshore waters. The prolonged period of NE winds will make it 
difficult for seas to subside.

&&

.ILM WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...Coastal Flood Advisory from 10 AM this morning to 2 PM EDT 
     this afternoon for NCZ107.
SC...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

FXUS62 KJAX 131409
AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
1009 AM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Moderate Rip Current Risk all Local Beaches Today and Friday.
Elevated Risk Returns Early Next Week

- Daily Heat Index up to 107 through Sunday

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms. Main Hazards: Locally
Heavy Rain, Lightning & Gusty Winds Up to 40-50 mph

&&

.UPDATE...

In the midst of pooled moisture ahead of trough has provided a near-
saturated upper air observation the morning, with measured 
precipitable water at 2.36" again which is not to far of from the 
statistical max for mid September (PWAT 2.38"). While there has been 
some slight cooling the in upper levels, which could support more 
frequent or excessive lightning, warming in the mid levels has also 
occurred, leading to weaker lapse rates and potential energy for 
thunderstorms later on today, mainly during the early afternoon.

The big picture remains the same, with dry northwesterly flow, 
associated with a shearing/dampening shortwave, making it into 
interior SE GA by this afternoon limiting thunderstorm activity 
while elsewhere there is a 30-60% chance of thunderstorms this 
afternoon and early evening. The primary focus for convection will 
once again be along the I-95 corridor with a near west-to-east 
steering flow in place acting the slow the Atlantic sea breeze and 
St Johns River breeze from advancing inland/westward.

As has been the situation regarding thunderstorm hazards over the 
last few days, frequent lightning, gusty outflow winds, and 
localized flooding are the primary concerns. Timing with CAMs has 
been relatively solid, indicating expanding shower development 
through 2 PM followed by scattered thunderstorm potential increasing 
thereafter as mesoscale boundaries and outflows interact.

Rain and thunderstorms will bring some relief in terms of 
temperature, but expect heat index to move quickly into the 100s by 
noon today as temperature rises into the low 90s. Drink plenty of 
water and seek shade during outdoor activities today and, as always, 
when thunder roars, head indoors.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH 12Z MONDAY/...
VFR conditions will continue through 13z with brief periods of 
broken MVFR ceilings at inland terminals (KJAX/KGNV/KVQQ) as low 
level moisture lifts. Surface winds will be light westerly with a 
sea breeze developing by 18z-20z for SSI, SGJ, and CRG switching 
winds to the southeast. Westerly steering winds aloft will push 
isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms toward the I-95 
corridor where stronger storms may develop due to sea breeze and 
outflow collisions. Localized IFR to LIFR conditions are possible 
due to heavy rain limiting visibility. Convective activity will fade 
after sunset with drier air limiting stratus and fog potential 
tonight for sites along and north of I-10 Monday morning.

&&

.MARINE...


Offshore winds will continue across the area waters today and on 
Monday, except for a sea breeze which will shift winds to the 
southeast and south during the afternoon hours. Another good chance 
of a couple of strong thunderstorms this afternoon and evening. 
Strong gusty winds and very heavy rainfall will accompany the 
stronger storms. On Monday, less thunderstorm activity is expected 
and likely be limited to northeast Florida nearshore waters. From 
Tuesday through Thursday, a strong northeast wind surge will bring 
small craft advisory conditions, rough seas, and numerous showers 
and a few thunderstorms over the area waters.

Rip Currents: Prevailing offshore winds (except for an afternoon 
sea breeze) and weak easterly swells will keep a low-end moderate 
risk of rip currents in effect the next couple of days. By Tuesday, 
strengthening northeast winds and building surf are expected which 
will continue into Thursday. This should result in a high rip 
current risk and dangerous surf at all area beaches during this time 
period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
     PATCHY TO AREAS OF HIGH DISPERSIONS TUESDAY THROUGH THURSDAY 
- Afternoons

A trough of low pressure will stretch across the southeastern US 
this weekend. High pressure will build to the northeast early next 
week, and strengthen through mid week. As this high builds, an 
inverted trough will develop east of the area. The gradient between 
these two features will result in elevated winds Tuesday through 
Thursday, especially at the coast. An inverted trough will settle 
overhead late in the week into the weekend. Daily thunderstorm 
chances are forecast, mainly in the afternoon and evening hours.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  92  73  94  73 /  10  10   0   0 
SSI  91  77  92  79 /  20  20   0   0 
JAX  92  75  93  75 /  40  20  10   0 
SGJ  91  76  91  76 /  40  30  10  10 
GNV  92  74  93  74 /  40  20  40  10 
OCF  92  75  93  74 /  50  20  50  20 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

FXUS65 KBOU 131133
AFDBOU

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
533 AM MDT Sun Sep 13 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Unseasonably warm along the Front Range and I-25 Corridor today. 

- Isolated to scattered high-based showers and thunderstorms with
  gusty winds late this afternoon and evening.

- Unsettled pattern this week, but plenty of uncertainty with
  regard to daily precipitation chances.

- Cooler weather arriving for Tuesday. Temperatures average around
  seasonal normals for latter half of the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Saturday/...
Issued at 240 AM MDT Sun Sep 13 2026

Flat upper level ridging is building across the forecast area as
evident in the latest water vapor imagery, as well temporary 
drying aloft. Meanwhile, a low level moisture surge of 
moisture/cooling was originating from the convective complex in 
the eastern portions of Kansas and Oklahoma. 

With the ridging aloft, we'll be heating up again with plenty of 
sunshine. Summer-like heat is expected to return for the Front 
Range and I-25 Corridor, with highs in the metro areas reaching 
the 90-95 degree range. There is more uncertainty about warming 
farther east across the eastern plains, given the weak surge noted
at the present time and also lack of lee troughing. A lot of the 
details hinge on the convective evolution in the Central Plains, 
but we do see cooler temps (highs closer to 80F) over the far 
northeast corner. With regard to convection, we do expect a late 
day/evening surge of mid/upper level moisture approaching from the
Desert Southwest. Given we'll likely warm dry adiabatically to 
550 mb and DCAPE increases to nearly 1500 J/kg, the main threat 
from any showers and storms late this afternoon and evening would 
be gusty microbursts. Peak winds could easily reach 50 mph given 
the DCAPE. We'll continue with the low PoPs in the forecast (very 
light rainfall) and added gusty winds as an attribute. 

Mid and upper level monsoonal moisture will continue to increase
late tonight through Monday morning, which will keep a chance of
showers in the forecast. By Monday afternoon, the deepest plume
shifts to areas southeast of I-76. At the same time, mid level
cloud cover could also limit daytime heating (still very warm!), 
and keep a weak cap in place for the afternoon. Thus, the 
development of afternoon storms may be limited to the mountains 
and Palmer Divide area. We do get into the right entrance region 
of an upper level jet, so that could help carry some convection 
east/northeast across the I-25 Corridor and plains through Monday 
evening. 

A stronger cold front is still on track to arrive Monday night,
ushering in much cooler weather for Tuesday. Guidance continues to
slowly slip for high temperatures, although we still think they 
may be too warm. While deterministic forecasts still lie in the
lower to mid 70s for the plains, forecast experience would 
suggest many locations of the plains would more likely (>60% 
chance) stay in the upper 60s. Of course this will depend heavily
on extent of post-frontal stratus. That cooling also means we'll 
be struggling to produce much instability, and any of that would 
have to come from the mid levels and/or convective initiation over
the mountains. Overall the chances of precipitation have 
decreased somewhat as the best plume of monsoonal moisture is now 
expected to stay to our south.

That may change as we head closer to Wednesday but more likely
Thursday or even Friday. Guidance suggests a slower approach of
the next trough moving across the northern Great Basin and Central
Rockies. In fact, this leads to considerable uncertainty for the
forecasts later this week, with Thursday now trending to be the 
wettest day (as hinted to yesterday). However, that trough is 
slowing so perhaps we could see daily chances of showers and 
storms last into next weekend. 

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS through 12Z Monday/...
Issued at 533 AM MDT Sun Sep 13 2026

S-SW winds at 10 kts or less are expected to turn more SE 
15Z-17Z, and then more easterly by 18Z-20Z. Wind speeds at KDEN 
should gradually increase to 10-14 kts after 21Z. 

The main concern will then shift to potential gusty outflow winds
from high based convection. We do see great enough confidence to 
maintain the TEMPO VRB G35kts, as DCAPE grows to 1500 J/kg and 
we'll likely reach full mixing to the high cloud bases (near
16,000 MSL) given strong heating. Today appears to be a slightly 
later convective day, with any threat (PROB30) holding off til 
22Z-23Z, and then greatest threat (TEMPO) 00Z-03Z. Given the  
magnitude of DCAPE, there's a slight (15-20%) chance of a brief 
G45 kts impacting the airports. 

Winds will settle down by/shortly after 03Z Monday and return to 
fairly normal diurnal wind patterns. Light showers are expected to
redevelop in the area (PROB30) after 13Z Monday. 

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
